title: Two Sum
statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Return the answer as two space-separated indices (0-indexed) in any order.

hints.text: A brute force double loop works but is slow for large n.
Store each value's index in a hash map while scanning once.

editorial: Use a hash map from value to index. For each element x, check if target - x was seen before.

reference_solutions.python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
n = int(data[0])
nums = list(map(int, data[1:1+n]))
target = int(data[1+n])
seen = {}
for i, v in enumerate(nums):
    if target - v in seen:
        print(seen[target - v], i)
        break
    seen[v] = i
